title: Abu al-Hasan of Khorasan

full_text:
Abu al-Hasan was an affluent merchant of the province of Khorasan whose palace stood beside the great Silk Road. His doors were never locked, and an illuminated lantern burned upon his terrace every night, welcoming travelers, scholars, and pilgrims to enjoy free lodging, savory banquets, and fresh horses without charge.

A political upheaval in Khorasan caused an oppressive governor to confiscate Abu al-Hasan’s estates on false charges, forcing the generous host to flee in disguise to Baghdad.

Penniless and wandering the bustling streets of the capital, Abu al-Hasan stopped before the grand emporium of a wealthy jewel merchant.

The jewel merchant looked out, recognized Abu al-Hasan, and rushed into the street with open arms! 'Welcome, master of Khorasan! Ten years ago, when I was an impoverished student freezing in the snow, your roof sheltered me for two months, and your purse paid for my journey!'

The jeweler brought Abu al-Hasan into his home, clothed him in silk robes, and introduced him to twenty other prominent merchants of Baghdad—all of whom had received his legendary hospitality in past years!

The merchants gathered together, raised thirty thousand gold dinars, and petitioned Caliph Harun al-Rashid.

The Caliph investigated the case, dismissed the corrupt governor of Khorasan, restored all Abu al-Hasan’s palaces and lands, and appointed him Governor of the province, demonstrating that bread cast upon the waters of hospitality returns as a fortress of protection in the hour of need.
moral: Boundless generosity toward travelers creates a network of friendship that shields a man in his hour of trial.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Abu Al-Hasan of Khorasan"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
